title: NeoRadar injector scenario
description: A scenario for tools/NeoRadar.Injector. Either the C++ SqwkstbyInjector group generator, or an explicit aircraft list, or both. A EuroScope sweatbox .txt converts to this shape with 'injector convert'.

routesFile.description: Path, relative to this file, of the {arrivals,departures} route file the group generator draws flight plans from. Default ./routes.json.

basePoint.description: Required when 'groups' is present, which the top-level if/then states. The first generated aircraft is one spacing step from here.

spacingKm.description: KILOMETRES between generated aircraft. The C++ tool passed this value to a metres API, so its spacing was 1000x smaller than the number written here.

spacingBearing.description: True bearing the generated aircraft are spread along.

groups.description: The C++ group generator. Flight plans are taken from the routes file round robin, not at random, so a scenario flies the same traffic every run.

airportAltitude.description: Field elevation in feet, the sweatbox AIRPORT_ALT record. The velocity packets report AGL against it when an aircraft carries no fieldElevation of its own.

metar.description: Replayed verbatim; there is no weather model. A sweatbox file may carry several METAR records.

ils.description: The sweatbox ILS<rwy> records, at most four. Either a heading or a far-end point the heading is derived from.

controllers.description: Parsed, recorded and ignored. The injector logs no controller in; the NeoRadar user is the only one.

namedRoutes.description: The sweatbox ROUTE records. Every point is resolved against the package like any other.

performance.description: The sweatbox PERFAC/PERFLINE tables, keyed by aircraft type. Overrides the shipped AircraftPerformance.txt for that type.

datalink.description: The aircraft half of a Hoppie exchange. At the top level it is the scenario-wide default; on an aircraft it overrides that per field. The injector uses its OWN logon code, from --hoppie-logon, injector.local.json or NEORADAR_INJECTOR_HOPPIE_LOGON, and never a code written into a scenario.

station.description: The controller Hoppie station callsign a request and a reply are addressed to, for example EGLL_DEL. Required once any other datalink field is set. It must not be an injected callsign: a poll is destructive per callsign.

requestAtSeconds.description: Sim seconds into the run at which the clearance request goes out.

requestText.description: The request wording. Default REQUEST PREDEP CLEARANCE <origin> TO <destination> STAND ---, which carries the PREDEP keyword NeoRadar classifies on.

requestType.description: How the request is sent. A real pilot client files a PDC request as a telex; NeoRadar classifies both the same way.

replyWith.description: The keyword the downlink carries once the uplink arrives. none never answers.

replyDelaySeconds.description: Sim seconds between the uplink and the reply. Absent means the aircraft own reaction delay is drawn, 12 to 17 s unless delaySeconds says otherwise.

pollIntervalSeconds.description: Sim seconds between polls while a request is outstanding, overriding the run default of 20.

instructionsAsDatalink.description: An INSTRUCTION line whose text carries a PDC keyword also goes out as a datalink request.

logon.description: Refused by the validator: a logon code is a secret and belongs in the credential chain, not in a scenario file.

datalinkFreeText.description: Free-text telexes at scripted sim times. An omitted recipient is the aircraft own station.

altitudeFeet.description: True altitude in feet. The validator rejects anything outside this range.

groundSpeedKt.description: Knots. The validator rejects anything outside this range; a sweatbox @ record often writes 0 for airborne traffic, which starts it at its profile speed.

squawk.description: Four octal digits. 0000 renders as a vehicle rather than an aircraft.

routePoints.description: A string is a bare name resolved against the package. An object may carry an explicit position instead, a per-point altitude, or an approach runway, which is the sweatbox trailing ILS<rwy> token and is never looked up.

mach.description: A fraction of the speed of sound. A sweatbox PERFLINE writes hundredths (078 is 0.78) and the parser normalises them; 0 means the row is an IAS row. The validator rejects 1 or more.

lines.description: Rows ascending by flight level. A row applies from its own level up to the next.

flightPlan.description: The 17-token $FP shape verbatim, because that is what goes on the wire and what NeoRadar parses back out. Every field is a string.

cruiseAltitude.description: Feet. A sweatbox FLxxx is normalised to feet on read.

delay.description: Seconds. A bare number is a fixed delay; the object form is a range the aircraft draws from. Omitting it is not a default of zero: a sweatbox block with no DELAY record gets 12 to 17 seconds on read.

instructions.description: The sweatbox INSTRUCTION records: a scripted pilot request sent as a #TM at a sim-time offset.

fieldElevation.description: Ground elevation beneath this aircraft, in feet. The velocity packets report AGL against it.

startAtSeconds.description: Seconds from scenario start before this aircraft appears. The sweatbox START record is minutes and is converted on read.

requestedAltitude.description: The sweatbox REQALT record. A bare number is feet from the start; the object form names the point the request applies at.

approach.description: The runway of a trailing ILS<rwy> token on the route. It must have a matching entry in 'ils'.

simData.description: The sweatbox SIMDATA record. Only maxTaxiSpeedKt and groundAltitudeFeet feed the model.

pseudoPilot.description: Recorded and ignored; one process owns every aircraft.

iasVariation.description: Per-aircraft speed offset in knots, drawn once per callsign and fixed for the run. The validator rejects anything above 20, as the EuroScope manual states.
